name: Storm-0501 (G1053) - AD Attack Chain (Week 10 hunt scope)
description: Enterprise techniques used by Storm-0501 (G1053), annotated for the group topic 'Threat Hunting for Active Directory Attacks'. Scores encode the role of each technique in the AD-to-cloud attack chain: 12 on-prem AD techniques, 19 cloud-pivot techniques. Built from the official MITRE layer (v1.0) - see data/storm0501_techniques.csv.

techniques.comment: Parent technique: Storm-0501 enumerated domain and cloud accounts
Used an obfuscated ADRecon variant to discover domain accounts (tools: ADRecon.ps1 (obfuscated obfs.ps1 / recon.ps1))
Enumerated users, roles and resources in Azure tenants (tools: AzureHound)
Parent technique: password resets and role elevation in the victim tenant
Reset passwords of admin accounts lacking MFA and registered own MFA method (tools: Password reset + own MFA registration)
Granted itself User Access Administrator and Owner roles over Azure subscriptions (tools: elevateAccess/action; roleAssignments/write)
Leveraged brute force attacks to obtain credentials
Enumerated cloud environments to identify critical assets and data stores (tools: AzureHound)
Discovered Azure policies, resource locks and storage immutability protections (tools: AzureHound)
Parent technique: extensive use of shell and scripting interpreters
Executed commands and scripts via PowerShell (tools: PowerShell; Evil-WinRM sessions)
Leveraged Cloud CLI to execute commands and exfiltrate data (tools: Azure CLI; AzCopy)
Parent technique: harvested credentials from password stores
Stole Keepass credentials using Find-KeePassConfig.ps1 (tools: Find-KeePassConfig.ps1)
Stored its encryption key in Azure Key Vault (tools: Azure Key Vault (KeyVault/vaults/write))
Destroyed data and backup files, including Azure storage accounts
Encrypted files using RaaS payloads; moved to cloud-based encryption scopes (tools: Sabbath; Hive; BlackCat; Hunters International; LockBit 3.0; Embargo)
Exposed non-remotely accessible storage accounts for collection (tools: storageAccounts/write)
Parent technique: developed own attacker capabilities
Used a self-signed TLS certificate imitating a Microsoft CA (tools: Self-signed 'Microsoft IT TLS CA 5' certificate)
Parent technique: tampered with domain GPOs and Entra tenant trust
Distributed GPOs to tamper with security products (tools: GPO distribution)
Added an attacker-controlled federated domain to sign in as any user via SAML (tools: AADInternals federated-domain backdoor)
Used nltest.exe to enumerate domain trusts (tools: nltest.exe)
Parent technique: exfiltrated data over web services
Exfiltrated data to MEGA, MegaSync and its own infrastructure (tools: MEGA; Rclone (svhost.exe); AzCopy)
Exploited N-days in ManageEngine, Citrix NetScaler, Adobe ColdFusion (tools: CVE-2022-47966; CVE-2023-4966; CVE-2023-29300/38203)
Engaged in double extortion and direct victim contact (tools: Double extortion; leak sites; Microsoft Teams contact)
Deleted snapshots, restore points, storage accounts and backup services (tools: snapshots/restorePoints/storageAccounts/RecoveryServices deletes)
Parent technique: masqueraded tooling on endpoints
Masqueraded Rclone as svhost.exe and scvhost.exe (tools: Rclone as svhost.exe / scvhost.exe)
Parent technique: tampered with identity authentication flows
Registered own MFA method and abused a hybrid-joined server to satisfy Conditional Access (tools: Own MFA registration; hybrid-joined device bypass)
Parent technique: modified victim cloud infrastructure
Deleted cloud data stores and resources across Azure subscriptions (tools: Mass deletion of Azure data stores)
Parent technique: obfuscated payloads and scripts
Packed Cobalt Strike payloads with Themida (tools: Themida-packed Cobalt Strike)
Parent technique: obtained malware and exploit capabilities
Obtained and weaponized N-day exploits for initial access (tools: N-day exploits (ManageEngine / NetScaler / ColdFusion))
Used the SecretsDump module to obtain account credentials (tools: Impacket SecretsDump)
Performed DCSync to extract credentials from the domain (tools: Impacket secretsdump.py / Mimikatz lsadump::dcsync)
Discovered running processes with tasklist.exe (tools: tasklist.exe)
Parent technique: used legitimate remote access tooling
Abused legitimate RMM tools for persistence and access (tools: AnyDesk; NinjaOne; Level.io)
Parent technique: moved laterally via remote services
Used Evil-WinRM (PowerShell over WinRM) for remote execution (tools: Evil-WinRM)
Used the compromised Entra Connect Sync server to move laterally (tools: Compromised Entra Connect Sync server)
Parent technique: abused scheduled tasks
Registered a SysUpdate task via GPO to distribute Embargo ransomware (tools: GPO-registered task 'SysUpdate')
Parent technique: discovered installed software
Checked for Defender for Endpoint services to target unprotected hosts (tools: sc query sense; sc query windefend)
Parent technique: abused signed binaries
Launched Cobalt Strike Beacons with regsvr32.exe (tools: regsvr32.exe (Cobalt Strike Beacon))
Launched Cobalt Strike Beacons with rundll32.exe (tools: rundll32.exe (Cobalt Strike Beacon))
Queried endpoint details with native tools and OSQuery (tools: systeminfo; OSQuery; ossec-win32)
Parent technique: checked victim system locale
Filtered out victims in prohibited language regions (Russia/CIS) (tools: CIS-language check)
Copied victim data to its own infrastructure with AzCopy (tools: AzCopy)
Parent technique: harvested exposed credentials
Stole Azure Storage access keys using the Owner role (tools: storageAccounts/listkeys/action)
Parent technique: abused valid accounts across environments
Abused the Entra Connect sync account, an MFA-less Global Admin and storage keys (tools: Entra Connect DSA; MFA-less Global Admin; storage keys)
